seoTitle: Can You Leave a Neon Sign On All the Time? Power & Cost
seoDescription: Can you leave an LED neon sign on all the time or overnight? Real wattage math, 24/7 electricity costs, thermal safety, and power supply longevity explained.
summary: Yes, modern 12V LED neon signs are completely safe to leave on 24/7 or overnight. They remain cool to the touch, draw only 20 to 70 watts (costing $1.00 to $3.50 a month at typical US electricity rates), and carry zero high-voltage fire risk. However, using a dimmer or smart plug extends the power adapter's lifespan significantly.

keyTakeaways: Modern LED neon signs run on 12V direct current and stay cool to the touch (typically 30°C to 38°C), making them safe to leave on continuously or overnight.
A typical 36-inch sign draws 35 to 50 watts, costing roughly $1.40 to $2.00 per month when operated 10 hours daily, or under $3.50 per month running 24/7 at US average electric rates.
Unlike vintage gas neon requiring 2,000V to 15,000V AC transformers, LED neon operates within Safety Extra-Low Voltage (SELV) limits with zero combustible gas or glass shatter risk.
While continuous illumination does not damage solid-state LEDs, it steadily consumes their 50,000-hour L70 lifespan and generates thermal wear on the AC/DC power adapter.
Pairing your sign with an inline dimmer set to 70% brightness or a simple $10 smart plug timer cuts power usage by 30% and roughly doubles the lifespan of your power driver.
